title: Frontend: Traffic Lights
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Traffic Lights. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Render [data-testid="light"] initially red. Advance follows red→green→amber→red. Pause toggles paused/running; Advance does nothing while paused. This tests a deterministic transition core, not a physical traffic-control system.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Represent the active light and a transition table containing the next state and duration.
alternativeApproaches: Introduce an all-red transition state and validate that no path activates conflicting lights.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Transition sequence; pause/resume policy; unmount.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
